metadata.Name: WINOGRANDE
metadata.Description: WINOGRANDE is a large-scale dataset of 44k problems inspired by the original Winograd Schema Challenge (WSC) design, but adjusted to improve both the scale and the hardness of the dataset. The dataset was created to investigate whether neural language models have truly acquired robust commonsense capabilities or whether they rely on spurious biases in the datasets.
metadata.Paper Title: WINOGRANDE: An Adversarial Winograd Schema Challenge at Scale
metadata.Abstract: The Winograd Schema Challenge (WSC) is a benchmark for commonsense reasoning, consisting of 273 expert-crafted pronoun resolution problems. Recent advances in neural language models have reached around 90% accuracy on variants of WSC, raising questions about whether these models have truly acquired robust commonsense capabilities or rely on spurious biases. To investigate this, we introduce WINOGRANDE, a large-scale dataset of 44k problems inspired by the original WSC design, but adjusted to improve both the scale and the hardness of the dataset. The key steps of the dataset construction consist of a carefully designed crowdsourcing procedure, followed by systematic bias reduction using a novel AFLITE algorithm that generalizes human-detectable word associations to machine-detectable embedding associations. The best state-of-the-art methods on WINOGRANDE achieve 59.4–79.1%, which are 15-35% below human performance of 94.0%, depending on the amount of the training data allowed. Furthermore, we establish new state-of-the-art results on five related benchmarks. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of WINOGRANDE when used as a resource for transfer learning, but also raise concerns about overestimating the true capabilities of machine commonsense across all these benchmarks.
